Subject: FintechAI / Redwood - Post-demo pricing & latency follow-up

Hi Samir — thanks again for your time on the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size pricing and pilot recommendations: 

Recap:
- Primary use case: real-time customer responses in the FintechAI mobile app (short prompts, 50-250 token completions typically).
- Current target: 200ms p95 for end-user responses, streaming preferred to keep UI snappy.
- Expected monthly volume (you mentioned rough numbers on the call): please confirm prompt vs completion split and peak qps.

Key qualification asks (so we can give a clean $/1M token estimate):
1) Monthly token volumes (monthly avg and peak month) and prompt vs completion token distribution (CSV is fine).
2) Target p95 latency SLO (100ms / 200ms / 300ms) — and whether 95th or 99th is most important.
3) Budget range or target unit economics (you mentioned aiming for ~$50 per 1M tokens; confirm if that's a hard target).

Latency vs cost tradeoffs (short summary):
- Hosted Standard tier (shared capacity): easiest to start, faster time-to-value. Latency/cost: roughly higher $/1M because we optimize for availability and general-purpose routing.
- Dedicated Reserved capacity: predictable throughput, lower unit cost at scale. Best when you need consistent p95 SLOs and predictable billing.
- Streaming reduces client-perceived latency but can increase per-token billable units slightly due to smaller, incremental network/compute overheads.
- Batching and KV/prefix caching: larger batch sizes reduce $/token but increase tail latency. Adaptive batching gives the best balance for interactive apps — we can tune batch windows to meet a 200ms p95 while still saving significant cost compared to per-request execution.

Initial pricing back-of-envelope (will refine after you send volumes):
- If you need 200ms p95 with streaming and 10M tokens/month: estimated $40-45 per 1M tokens on Dedicated (dependent on exact prompt/completion mix).
- Hosted Standard for same profile: estimated $55-75 per 1M tokens.

Attachments: I'm including a quick sample CSV format (FintechAI_usage_sample.csv) — please fill with a few days of traffic (timestamps, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens) so we can model batching and cost.

Next steps:
- Send the token distribution CSV and confirm target SLO and budget range.
- If budget/SLO look aligned we'll propose a 2-week canary pilot (can be Dedicated burst or Hosted with guaranteed capacity) and a mutual action plan (MAAP).

Thanks — I'll loop in Jordan and Dev to scope implementation needs once we have the numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole

- Volume: We expect ~10M tokens/month initially, growing to ~30-40M within 6-9 months if conversions track. Peak month could be ~60M. Attached is a short requirements doc.
- Prompt vs completion: Approx 30% prompt / 70% completion by token count (many short prompts, longer responses).
- Peak QPS: 35-45 qps at peak (mobile burst patterns).
- SLO: 200ms p95 is our stated target for launch; 100ms would be ideal but not required initially. We prioritize p95 over p99.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is important for our UX — we'd like to keep that.
- Budget: Our finance/ops team is aiming for ~$50 per 1M tokens as a target unit economics number. There's some flexibility for first 3 months for a pilot.

Questions for you:
1) Can you provide a simple comparison table for Dedicated Reserved vs Hosted Standard showing expected $/1M tokens at 10M and 30M volumes for the 200ms p95 streaming profile?
2) What are typical batching configurations you'd recommend for this use case (batch windows, max batch size) to stay within 200ms p95?
3) What telemetry/tracing should our engineering team instrument for the pilot?

Thanks — I can loop in our contracts email (contracts@fintechai.com) once we have a ballpark pricing and MAAP.

Samir — thanks for the details, very helpful. Below is a concise comparison and proposed pilot plan.

Quick $/1M token comparison (streaming, 200ms p95 target, estimates):
- Dedicated Reserved (recommended for predictable p95):
  - 10M/mo: ~$45 per 1M tokens (we achieve this with a reserved pool + adaptive batching + KV caching for prompt prefixes)
  - 30M/mo: ~$35-40 per 1M tokens (scale drives better GPU utilization and lower kernel overhead)
- Hosted Standard (shared; faster provisioning, slightly higher cost):
  - 10M/mo: ~$60 per 1M tokens
  - 30M/mo: ~$50-60 per 1M tokens

Batching guidance to meet 200ms p95 with streaming:
- Adaptive batching window of 8-15ms plus a max batch size of 8-16 for your payload distribution. This usually keeps model latency within a 150-220ms p95 envelope while reducing $/token by ~20-35% compared to single-request execution.
- Use prefix KV caching for repeated system/context tokens to cut compute by ~10-15%.

Telemetry suggestions (for pilot):
- Token-level billing events (tokens generated per request) exported to your analytics.
- P95/P99 latency per route and per model variant.
- Streaming chunk timing (time-to-first-byte and complete-stream) to validate UX improvements.
- Batch size distribution and queueing delay metrics.

Pilot proposal (2-week canary):
1) Setup a small Dedicated Reserved pool (can start with burst-enabled reserved nodes) and enable streaming + adaptive batching.
2) Redwood runs a short perf run using a 48-hour sample and we'll tune batch window to hit 200ms p95.
3) Deliver a short MAAP and an SOW for the pilot (attached: Pilot_SOW.docx, HighLevel_Pricing.xlsx).

Ballpark next steps & timeline:
- If this looks good, I'll send a MAAP and we can target the pilot start as early as Aug 24.
- During the pilot we'll collect telemetry and produce a cost projection for 1M/10M/30M tokens with the tuned batch/stream config.

If you want, I can also propose a simple billing cap for the pilot so finance has comfort on spend.

Best,
Marissa
